title: Chapter I — Off Campus Living: A Famous Debate
text:
Chapter I
Off Campus Living

A FAMOUS DEBATE

On April 18, 1890, a debate was held between the Savoy and Whitewright schools on the subject of "Resolved that the negro should be removed to Africa, in peace if we can, by force if we must." Speakers on the affirmative side representing the Savoy school were J. B. Thompson of Marysville, Texas, and James C. Wells of Bells, Texas. On the negative side, representing the Whitewright school, were E. N. Williamson of Shreveport, La., and G. W. Truett of Haynesville, N. C. This G. W. Truett is the present Dr. George W. Truett, pastor of the First Baptist Church at Dallas and world-wide eminent church statesman. When the old program of the debate in question was shown to him he acknowledged same in these words:

"Promptly replying, I beg to thank you most cordially for the distinct courtesy you have done me in sending me a copy of the old program of the debate between the two schools at Savoy and Whitewright, April 18, 1890. The sight of the old program that you sent me awakens the most vivid recollections of that very interesting occasion, when the debate was had. I recall that a big train load of people came over from the Savoy school to Whitewright, where the debate was had. I recall, too, that a member of the faculty was the one who took up the discussion on the other side, and we were all closer friends than ever because of the occasion.

"Yes, I remember quite well the fine and far-reaching influence of the College at Savoy, under the presidency of Robert R. Halsell. There is literally no computation of the far-reaching good done by such schools as the ones at Savoy and Whitewright a generation and more ago. Out land will always be deeply indebted to such teachers as those schools had."
notes: Recounts the April 18, 1890 inter-school debate; quotes a letter from Dr. George W. Truett, later famous Dallas First Baptist pastor, who participated as a student.
